clients.name: Margaret
clients.label: Cautious
clients.story: Just retired and nervous about losing money, so she was placed in the most cautious model, with only 20% in shares.
clients.goal: Draw about £24,000 a year, rising with inflation, for a 30-year retirement without running out of money.
clients.decision: Take more market risk, not less, to cut the risk of the pot running dry.
clients.note:
Dear Margaret,

Your portfolio is profiled at the most cautious end, and on the measure most people mean by risk it is calm. It moves around less and falls less far than a bolder mix. But the risk that matters most to you is a different one, whether the money lasts. On our simulations the most cautious mix funds your full 30 years about 75% of the time. A more balanced mix raises that to roughly 92%.

The trade is real. You would see bigger swings along the way, with a worst historical fall nearer 36% than 18%. In exchange you cut the chance of running short later in retirement. For a 30-year plan drawing 4%, that is a trade I would recommend making.

clients.name: Tom
clients.label: Balanced
clients.story: Saving hard for a first house. Profiled balanced, which sounds safe for a six-year plan.
clients.goal: Turn £40,000 plus £500 a month into a house deposit in about six years.
clients.decision: Do not lean on the bond cushion the way the label assumes, and de-risk toward the goal as the date nears.
clients.note:
Dear Tom,

Balanced sounds safe for a six-year plan, and over the long run the label is not wrong. The catch is the bond half. It is meant to steady things when shares fall, but in 2022 bonds and shares fell together, and right now they are still moving in step (correlation +0.42).

Today your balanced mix reaches the deposit about 64% of the time. As your purchase date gets close I would step the risk down. That lowers the headline chance, to nearer 51%, but it protects the money you have already built from a bad final year, the kind that bonds may not cushion the way the label assumes. Close to the date, keeping the deposit matters more than reaching for a bigger one.

clients.name: Priya
clients.label: Adventurous
clients.story: Long horizon, high tolerance, profiled adventurous. Her equity sleeve has quietly drifted into a semiconductor-heavy bet.
clients.goal: Grow wealth over the long run without carrying risk she did not choose and does not know about.
clients.decision: Trim the concentration she did not know she was carrying back toward a diversified adventurous portfolio.
clients.note:
Dear Priya,

You are happy with a bold portfolio, and that is fine. The issue is not how much risk you are taking but what kind. Your equity has drifted into a heavy semiconductor position. Two adventurous investors can look identical on a risk label and hold very different real risk. Your concentrated version fell about 39% in the 2021 to 2022 sell-off, against about 26% for a diversified adventurous mix.

The wider market is not unusually concentrated today, so this is not a warning about a bubble. It is about the position you already hold. My recommendation is to trim the concentration back toward a diversified holding, so you keep the risk you chose and lose the risk you drifted into.
